messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

My question is actually R-adjacent... I'd like the final product to be a single directory of .txt files that I can read and rbind in R, but my hunch is that the best tool for the file-moving job is the shell.

I was given an external hard drive with a dataset of files, associated metadata, other crap, etc., that are organized by site-- so the directory structure is like this (there is actually 1 more subdirectory within Site, but this is basically it):

Volumes/Aves/DATA
  ->Site 1
     ->OtherData
     -> TheDataIWant
  ->Site 2
     ->OtherData
     -> TheDataIWant
  ->... Site X
     ->OtherData
     -> TheDataIWant

I want to copy all .txt files from the subdirectories named "TheDataIWant", and paste them into a new directory on my own machine (let's call it "/users/mary/Desktop/DENA").

A couple other considerations: Site information is retained in the filenames themselves, so I don't have to worry about losing important metadata by collapsing the file structure. There is also other crap in the "TheDataIWant" folder besides the txt files, which I do NOT want to copy.

I googled this question and couldn't find an answer that I understood, because I am sadly not fluent in the shell. So I would be extra grateful for a response that also explained what each bit of syntax is doing!

Thanks,
Mary

I was trying to do something similar recently, and the hack solution I found was (for once) straightforward and code-less. Not sure if this would work on a mac, but on a PC:  have your destination location open in one Windows Explorer window and the Volumes/Aves/DATA root folder open in another folder. Use the search bar next to the file path bar to search for "txt", and it should bring up all of the .txt files in the subdirectory (should say "Search Results in DATA" or something similar in the file path bar)--you can copy everything in the window into a destination folder from there.

Cheers,
Leah

messages.subject_clean: Package data unavailable until after calling library(package_name)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm having trouble with making some package data available both to functions within a package and to users of the package, without forcing them to call "library(my_package)" first. I have a detailed description, followed by my question and a link to a reproducible example below.

We've been developing a package (let's call it myPackageTest) that needs access to some a precalculated data frame (call it public_data).

This data is stored as a .rda file in the data folder of the package. It is documented in the data.R file in the data folder of the package.

If I open a clean R workspace and run the command myPackageTest::public_data, without running library(myPackageTest) first, it works and I can see the data frame. Great!

However, I have function my_function which relies on public_data. If I then call myPackageTest::my_function(), I get:

Error in myPackageTest::my_function() :
  object 'public_data' not found

If I call library(myPackageTest), then repeat my call to my_function(), everything works and the data is found.

If I switch the format of the data to .Rdata from .rda, as Hadley Wickham's package guide says we should, then it's available nowhere, not even after calling "library(myPackageTest".

I've been able to make it so that package functions can access the data whether the user has called "library" or not by switching the data to internal data stored in sysdata.rda, but then the data isn't available directly to package users if I want them to have it too. I haven't seen anything indicating that data the package exports isn't available within the package (but I'm beginning to suspect this)

So, my question - is there a solution that makes package data:
work within package functions without the need to use "library(myPackageTest)" (I want other R libraries to be able to use it that can't/shouldn't call "library")
makes the data available to users of the package
Maybe I'm looking at this wrong? The real code and a minimal reproducible example that matches what I've shared here are both stored at https://github.com/ceff-tech/ffc_api_client/tree/packageTest

Thanks for any help you can provide - I hope my question and problem description are clear - I'd be happy to clarify anything.

Nick Santos
UC Davis Center for Watershed Sciences <http://watershed.ucdavis.edu>
nrsa...@ucdavis.edu, 530-754-9362

So, I seem to have run into a mysterious problem installing the "stringr" package that no one else in my 'R' class had, and the teacher was rather puzzled.

install.packages("stringr")

library(stringr)

also installing the dependency ‘stringi’

Dear All,

We are pleased to announce our first annual call for nominations for D-RUG Coordinators. Our coordinators work together to fulfill the mission of Davis R Users Group: to foster a community of R-Users at UC Davis who support each other in using  <https://cran.r-project.org/>R for science and research. Our coordinators are dedicated to providing a welcoming and supportive environment for all people, regardless of background or identity. We currently have four coordinator roles and are accepting nominations for all four positions: Email List Coordinator, Working Group Coordinator, Website Coordinator, and Administrative Coordinator. Please see the attached document for a description of the roles. Feel free to contact any of the current coordinators with questions about their roles!

We encourage self-nominations. If you nominate someone other than yourself, please check with them first to make sure this is a role they would be willing to fill.

New coordinators will be selected from the pool of nominees by our current coordinators.

We are providing a link to a google form below for submission of nominations. The form includes descriptions of current coordinator roles and responsibilities. Please submit nominations by January 31, 2020. We will announce new coordinators by February 14, 2020.

Google form: https://forms.gle/uWAQJ5P6AdkRF9jn9

In the past, coordinator turnover generally occurred as coordinators moved away from Davis. To encourage community involvement and retention of institutional knowledge, we are beginning an annual nomination process. We use the four roles we have outlined to make D-RUG work right now, but we expect D-RUG and coordinator roles to evolve with the needs of the community and with the interests of the specific coordinators.

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I posted this question in the MAD.oxli when I first encountered it yesterday, and think I understand a little more what is missing now but still not sure how to solve it.

I ran a snakefile to align my 3'tag-seq data using Salmon, and in the process of the alignment removed some lines of code.

Upon performing the count file generation step using tximport in R, I realized I don't have a count file folder - just a quant.sf file for each individual subject sequenced.

The region highlighted in yellow prompts the error message:
Error in all(file.exists(files)) : invalid 'file' argument
In addition: Warning message:
Unknown or uninitialised column: 'files'.

And the region highlighted in green is where I think I've made a mistake. I thought the tx2gene file was the location of the annotated transcriptome, and hoped that the fact that my alignment did not generate anything with tx2gene would be OK.

This is my code, with any changes i've made to fit the code in red, and the original code in blue:

# Install the latest version of DEseq2
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")

# load the library
source("https://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")

BiocManager::install("TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene")

BiocManager::install("tximport")

library(tximport)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# read in file names
files <- read_csv("samples_FXTAS_nonribo.csv")

### read in human counts
#original code
tx2gene <- read_tsv("outputs/tx2gene/dogtx2gene.tsv")
canine <- tximport(files = files$files, type = "salmon", tx2gene = tx2gene)
caninecounts <- canine$counts

#my code to work with human transcriptome
library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene)
txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene

messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I'm working on a research project to be able to identify, label, and/or segment the individual notes in audio recordings of bird songs (the Cassin's Finch specifically). I have .wav files of each possible individual note that has been previously identified but have many recordings that need to still be labeled with their respective notes. Currently I've been trying to work with a Python package called pyAudioAnalysis that would theoretically allow me to feed in the .wav files of the individual notes to train the program to identify them in larger recordings of songs that have not yet had their notes labeled. However, this has been rife with issues and I was wondering if there was anything R-based that could perform a similar function of identifying, labeling, and/or segmenting these audio files.

The ultimate goal is to have a large collection of each note from different individuals identified and separated. Because male Cassin's Finches display the unique behavior of utilizing pieces of other birds' songs in their own, presumably for the purpose of mating, the goal is to create audio files composed of these separated notes that will be played back to female Cassin's Finches to see how they respond to different compositions of notes.

Hopefully the question and purpose of the project make sense, but please feel free to ask if anything needs clarification. Thank you for your help!

All the best,

Parish Bracha
